units.name: public metadata and value accessors
units.summary: Public metadata and value accessors.
units.explain: Public metadata and value accessors. The error pointer returns the global error buffer plus its recorded position without a null guard. The string getter returns the stored string only for a string item, otherwise NULL; the number getter returns the stored double only for a number item, otherwise NAN.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(const char *) cJSON_GetErrorPtr(void)

units.name: case_insensitive_strcmp
units.summary: Case-insensitive comparison of two byte strings.
units.explain: Case-insensitive comparison of two byte strings. It returns 1 if either pointer is NULL, so two NULL pointers are not equal; returns 0 for the same pointer; otherwise compares lowercased bytes until a difference or the terminating NUL and returns the lowercased byte difference.
units.sig: static int case_insensitive_strcmp(const unsigned char *string1, const unsigned char *string2)

units.name: allocation hooks and item lifecycle
units.summary: Allocation hooks and item lifecycle.
units.explain: Allocation hooks and item lifecycle. The internal wrappers forward to malloc, free, and realloc. The duplicate helper returns NULL for NULL input, allocates strlen plus one through the supplied hooks, copies, and returns NULL on allocation failure.
units.sig: static void * CJSON_CDECL internal_malloc(size_t size)

units.name: get_decimal_point
units.summary: Returns the current locale decimal point first byte when locale support is enabled, otherwise a period.
units.explain: Returns the current locale decimal point first byte when locale support is enabled, otherwise a period.
units.sig: static unsigned char get_decimal_point(void)

units.name: parse_number
units.summary: Parses a numeric token from the parse buffer.
units.explain: Parses a numeric token from the parse buffer. It returns false for a NULL buffer or content. It scans digits, signs, e/E, and period until another byte, allocates a temporary string, replaces periods with the locale decimal point, and calls strtod.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool parse_number(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_buffer)

units.name: cJSON_SetNumberHelper
units.summary: Sets a number item's double and saturated integer fields.
units.explain: Sets a number item's double and saturated integer fields. A NULL object returns NAN. Values at or above INT_MAX saturate to INT_MAX; values at or below INT_MIN saturate to INT_MIN; otherwise the integer is the cast value.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(double) cJSON_SetNumberHelper(cJSON *object, double number)

units.name: cJSON_SetValuestring
units.summary: Replaces a string item's value under strict preconditions.
units.explain: Replaces a string item's value under strict preconditions. It returns NULL unless the object is a non-reference string with a non-NULL existing valuestring and the new string is non-NULL.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(char*) cJSON_SetValuestring(cJSON *object, const char *valuestring)

units.name: ensure
units.summary: Ensures a print buffer has room for a requested byte count.
units.explain: Ensures a print buffer has room for a requested byte count. It returns NULL for a NULL buffer state or NULL backing buffer. The offset-at-or-past-length guard applies only when length is greater than zero, so a zero-length buffer with offset zero is not rejected there.
units.sig: static unsigned char* ensure(printbuffer * const p, size_t needed)

units.name: update_offset
units.summary: Advances a print buffer offset by the length of the NUL-terminated string at its current offset.
units.explain: Advances a print buffer offset by the length of the NUL-terminated string at its current offset. It does nothing for a NULL buffer state or NULL backing buffer.
units.sig: static void update_offset(printbuffer * const buffer)

units.name: compare_double
units.summary: Compares two doubles using an absolute tolerance of the larger magnitude times DBL_EPSILON.
units.explain: Compares two doubles using an absolute tolerance of the larger magnitude times DBL_EPSILON.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool compare_double(double a, double b)

units.name: print_number
units.summary: Renders a number item into a print buffer.
units.explain: Renders a number item into a print buffer. A NULL output buffer returns false. NaN or infinity writes null.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_number(const cJSON * const item, printbuffer * const output_buffer)

units.name: parse_hex4
units.summary: Parses exactly four hexadecimal digits.
units.explain: Parses exactly four hexadecimal digits. It returns zero if any digit is invalid; otherwise it accumulates the four nibbles into an unsigned value.
units.sig: static unsigned parse_hex4(const unsigned char * const input)

units.name: utf16_literal_to_utf8
units.summary: Converts one UTF-16 escape, or a surrogate pair, to UTF-8.
units.explain: Converts one UTF-16 escape, or a surrogate pair, to UTF-8. It fails with zero if fewer than six bytes remain, if the first code is a low surrogate, if a high surrogate lacks a following backslash-u sequence or valid low surrogate, or if the codepoint exceeds 0x10FFFF.
units.sig: static unsigned char utf16_literal_to_utf8(const unsigned char * const input_pointer, const unsigned char * const input_end, unsigned char **output_pointer)

units.name: parse_string
units.summary: Parses a quoted JSON string into a newly allocated value.
units.explain: Parses a quoted JSON string into a newly allocated value. It fails if the current byte is not an opening quote, if the closing quote is missing, if a trailing backslash runs past the buffer, on allocation failure, on an unknown escape, or on failed UTF-16 conversion.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool parse_string(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_buffer)

units.name: print_string_ptr
units.summary: Writes a quoted, escaped string into a print buffer.
units.explain: Writes a quoted, escaped string into a print buffer. A NULL output buffer returns false. A NULL input writes an empty quoted string and returns true.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_string_ptr(const unsigned char * const input, printbuffer * const output_buffer)

units.name: print_string
units.summary: Delegates string printing to the string pointer printer using the item's valuestring.
units.explain: Delegates string printing to the string pointer printer using the item's valuestring.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_string(const cJSON * const item, printbuffer * const p)

units.name: buffer_skip_whitespace
units.summary: Skips bytes up to and including whitespace at the current offset.
units.explain: Skips bytes up to and including whitespace at the current offset. It returns NULL for a NULL buffer or content. If no byte is accessible it returns the buffer unchanged.
units.sig: static parse_buffer *buffer_skip_whitespace(parse_buffer * const buffer)

units.name: skip_utf8_bom
units.summary: Skips a UTF-8 BOM at the start of a parse buffer.
units.explain: Skips a UTF-8 BOM at the start of a parse buffer. It returns NULL for a NULL buffer or content or when the offset is not zero. It skips three bytes only when index four is accessible and the first three bytes are EF BB BF; a short BOM-prefixed buffer is therefore not skipped.
units.sig: static parse_buffer *skip_utf8_bom(parse_buffer * const buffer)

units.name: parse entrypoints
units.summary: Public parse entrypoints.
units.explain: Public parse entrypoints. The options wrapper returns NULL immediately for a NULL value before delegating, so that failure does not go through the core parser error handling; otherwise it passes strlen plus one to the length parser.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON *) cJSON_ParseWithOpts(const char *value, const char **return_parse_end, cJSON_bool require_null_terminated)

units.name: print entrypoints
units.summary: Public print entrypoints.
units.explain: Public print entrypoints. The core printer allocates a 256-byte buffer through hooks, records format and hooks, prints the value, updates the offset, then either reallocates to offset plus one or allocates a new buffer, copies the smaller of length and offset plus one, NUL-terminates, and frees the old buffer.
units.sig: static unsigned char *print(const cJSON * const item, cJSON_bool format, const internal_hooks * const hooks)

units.name: parse_value
units.summary: Dispatches one JSON value from the parse buffer.
units.explain: Dispatches one JSON value from the parse buffer. It returns false for a NULL buffer or content. It recognizes null, false, and true only when enough bytes are readable and the literal matches, setting the type and advancing the offset.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool parse_value(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_buffer)

units.name: print_value
units.summary: Dispatches one item to its printer.
units.explain: Dispatches one item to its printer. It returns false for a NULL item or output buffer. Null, false, and true ensure space and copy their literals.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_value(const cJSON * const item, printbuffer * const output_buffer)

units.name: parse_array
units.summary: Parses a JSON array into a linked child list.
units.explain: Parses a JSON array into a linked child list. It fails immediately when nesting depth is at the limit. It increments depth, requires a left bracket, skips whitespace, accepts an empty right bracket, and otherwise steps back and loops allocating items, linking them, parsing each value, and skipping whitespace after commas.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool parse_array(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_buffer)

units.name: print_array
units.summary: Renders an array into a print buffer.
units.explain: Renders an array into a print buffer. It returns false for a NULL output buffer or when nesting depth is at the limit. It writes a left bracket, increments depth, prints each child, updates the offset, and between children writes a comma plus a space only in formatted mode.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_array(const cJSON * const item, printbuffer * const output_buffer)

units.name: parse_object
units.summary: Parses a JSON object into a linked child list.
units.explain: Parses a JSON object into a linked child list. It fails immediately when nesting depth is at the limit.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool parse_object(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_buffer)

units.name: print_object
units.summary: Renders an object into a print buffer.
units.explain: Renders an object into a print buffer. It returns false for a NULL output buffer or when nesting depth is at the limit. It writes a left brace and, in formatted mode, a newline, then increments depth.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool print_object(const cJSON * const item, printbuffer * const output_buffer)

units.name: array accessors
units.summary: Array size and item access.
units.explain: Array size and item access. Size returns zero for a NULL array, otherwise counts the child chain and casts to int, with possible overflow. The internal item getter returns NULL for a NULL array, walks next links index times, and returns the reached child or NULL.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(int) cJSON_GetArraySize(const cJSON *array)

units.name: object lookup
units.summary: Object member lookup.
units.explain: Object member lookup. The internal lookup returns NULL for a NULL object or name, walks the child chain, and compares names either case-sensitively with strcmp or case-insensitively with the case-insensitive comparator. It returns NULL when no match is found or the matched child has a NULL string, otherwise the child.
units.sig: static cJSON *get_object_item(const cJSON * const object, const char * const name, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: array append and references
units.summary: Array append and reference creation.
units.explain: Array append and reference creation. The suffix helper links a previous item to a new item. Reference creation returns NULL for a NULL item or allocation failure; otherwise it copies the item, clears its string, marks it as a reference, and clears next and prev.
units.sig: static void suffix_object(cJSON *prev, cJSON *item)

units.name: object insertion
units.summary: Object insertion with key ownership.
units.explain: Object insertion with key ownership. The const-cast helper returns a mutable pointer. The internal inserter returns false for NULL object, key, or item, or when object and item are the same.
units.sig: static void* cast_away_const(const void* string)

units.name: reference insertion
units.summary: Adds a reference copy of an item to an array or object.
units.explain: Adds a reference copy of an item to an array or object. Array insertion returns false for a NULL array, otherwise appends the created reference; a NULL reference makes the append fail. Object insertion returns false for a NULL object or key, otherwise inserts the created reference with a non-constant key.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON_bool) cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray(cJSON *array, cJSON *item)

units.name: typed object adders
units.summary: Convenience adders for typed object members.
units.explain: Convenience adders for typed object members. Each creates a null, true, false, bool, number, string, raw, object, or array item, inserts it with a non-constant key, and returns the created item on success. On insertion failure it deletes the created item and returns NULL.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON*) cJSON_AddNullToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)

units.name: detach and delete items
units.summary: Detaches or deletes array and object members.
units.explain: Detaches or deletes array and object members. Pointer detach returns NULL for NULL parent or item, or when the item is not the first child and has no prev. It unlinks from neighbors, updates the parent child when first, updates the tail pointer when last, clears the item links, and returns the item.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON *) cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer(cJSON *parent, cJSON * const item)

units.name: insert and replace items
units.summary: Inserts and replaces array or object members.
units.explain: Inserts and replaces array or object members. Array insert rejects negative index or NULL new item, appends when the index is past the end, rejects a non-first item with no prev, otherwise links before the found item and updates the child when needed.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON_bool) cJSON_InsertItemInArray(cJSON *array, int which, cJSON *newitem)

units.name: basic item creators
units.summary: Basic item creators.
units.explain: Basic item creators. Each allocates a zeroed item through global hooks and sets its type. Number also stores the double and a saturated integer.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON *) cJSON_CreateNull(void)

units.name: array creators from c arrays
units.summary: Creates arrays from C arrays of ints, floats, doubles, or strings.
units.explain: Creates arrays from C arrays of ints, floats, doubles, or strings. Each returns NULL for a negative count or NULL source. It creates an array, then for each element creates a number or string item; creation failure deletes the array and returns NULL.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON *) cJSON_CreateIntArray(const int *numbers, int count)

units.name: duplication
units.summary: Duplicates a cJSON tree.
units.explain: Duplicates a cJSON tree. The public wrapper starts recursion at depth zero. The recursive worker returns NULL for a NULL item or allocation failure.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON *) cJSON_Duplicate(const cJSON *item, cJSON_bool recurse)

units.name: minification
units.summary: Minifies JSON text in place.
units.explain: Minifies JSON text in place. The one-line comment skipper advances past two slashes and then through the newline or to NUL. The multiline skipper advances past slash-star and through star-slash or to NUL.
units.sig: static void skip_oneline_comment(char **input)

units.name: type predicates
units.summary: Type predicates.
units.explain: Type predicates. Each returns false for a NULL item. The specific predicates compare the low byte of the type to invalid, false, true, null, number, string, array, object, or raw.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON_bool) cJSON_IsInvalid(const cJSON * const item)

units.name: cJSON_Compare
units.summary: Deep structural comparison.
units.explain: Deep structural comparison. It returns false for NULL inputs or differing low-byte types, and false for types outside the supported set. Identical pointers are equal.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(cJSON_bool) cJSON_Compare(const cJSON * const a, const cJSON * const b, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: cjson malloc
units.summary: Allocation wrappers.
units.explain: Allocation wrappers. The malloc wrapper delegates to the global allocate hook. The free wrapper delegates to the global deallocate hook and then clears its local pointer copy, which does not affect the caller's pointer.
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(void *) cJSON_malloc(size_t size)

units.name: platform and visibility macros
units.summary: Selects calling convention and symbol visibility for the public API.
units.explain: Selects calling convention and symbol visibility for the public API. __WINDOWS__ is auto-defined when not already set and any of WIN32, WIN64, _MSC_VER, or _WIN32 is defined.
units.sig: #define __WINDOWS__

units.name: cJSON
units.summary: Defines the JSON node structure used by the API.
units.explain: Defines the JSON node structure used by the API. next and prev link sibling nodes; child points to the first child of an array or object; type holds the node type flags; valuestring holds string or raw text; valueint is deprecated and valuedouble holds numeric value; string holds the object member name when the node is an objec…
units.sig:
struct cJSON
struct cJSON
cJSON

units.name: cJSON_Hooks
units.summary: Holds allocator hooks for cJSON.
units.explain: Holds allocator hooks for cJSON. malloc_fn and free_fn are function pointers using CJSON_CDECL, so Windows callers can pass CDECL malloc/free directly. The InitHooks comment mentions realloc, but this struct exposes only malloc and free hooks; no realloc field is present.
units.sig: struct cJSON_Hooks

units.name: limits and bool type
units.summary: Defines the boolean type and compile-time parse limits.
units.explain: Defines the boolean type and compile-time parse limits. cJSON_bool is int. CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT defaults to 1000 and CJSON_CIRCULAR_LIMIT defaults to 10000 unless already defined; the comments say parsing rejects deeper nesting or longer circular references to prevent stack overflows.
units.sig: #define CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT 1000

units.name: cJSON.h
units.summary: Declares the main cJSON API for parsing, printing, traversal, creation, mutation, comparison, and minification.
units.explain: Declares the main cJSON API for parsing, printing, traversal, creation, mutation, comparison, and minification.

units.name: value setters
units.summary: Groups macros and declarations that change a node value.
units.explain: Groups macros and declarations that change a node value. cJSON_SetIntValue: if object is non-NULL, assigns both valueint and valuedouble to number and yields the assigned value; if NULL, yields number without assignment. cJSON_SetNumberValue: if object is non-NULL, calls cJSON_SetNumberHelper with the number cast to double and…
units.sig: #define cJSON_SetIntValue(object, number) ((object) ? (object)->valueint = (object)->valuedouble = (number) : (number))

units.name: cJSON.h
units.summary: Declares the array iteration macro and allocator entry points.
units.explain: Declares the array iteration macro and allocator entry points. cJSON_ArrayForEach initializes element to NULL when array is NULL, otherwise to array->child, and advances through next until NULL. cJSON_malloc and cJSON_free are declared to allocate and free using the hooks set by cJSON_InitHooks; their implementations are not in…

units.name: cJSONUtils_strdup
units.summary: Allocates a NUL-terminated copy of a byte string using the project allocator.
units.explain: Allocates a NUL-terminated copy of a byte string using the project allocator. Returns NULL if allocation fails; otherwise copies length plus terminator. It does not check for a NULL input before strlen and memcpy, so that input is outside its handled boundary.
units.sig: static unsigned char* cJSONUtils_strdup(const unsigned char* const string)

units.name: compare_strings
units.summary: Compares two byte strings with optional case folding and treats any NULL operand as unequal.
units.explain: Compares two byte strings with optional case folding and treats any NULL operand as unequal. - Either pointer NULL: return 1. - Identical pointers: return 0. - Case-sensitive: return strcmp result. - Case-insensitive: scan with tolower until terminator, returning 0 if both end together, otherwise the tolower difference.
units.sig: static int compare_strings(const unsigned char *string1, const unsigned char *string2, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: compare_double
units.summary: Tests floating-point equality within a relative epsilon.
units.explain: Tests floating-point equality within a relative epsilon. Computes max absolute operand, then returns whether absolute difference is at most that max times DBL_EPSILON. Both zero compare equal; NaN operands make the comparison false.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool compare_double(double a, double b)

units.name: compare_pointers
units.summary: Matches one JSON-pointer path token against an object key, honoring ~0 and ~1 escapes and optional case folding.
units.explain: Matches one JSON-pointer path token against an object key, honoring ~0 and ~1 escapes and optional case folding. - NULL operand: false. - Invalid escape: false. - Character mismatch: false. - One side ends before the other: false. A token ends at NUL or slash; case-sensitive mode uses exact bytes, otherwise tolower.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool compare_pointers(const unsigned char *name, const unsigned char *pointer, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: pointer_encoded_length
units.summary: Computes the encoded length of a string as a JSON-pointer token, counting one extra byte for each tilde or slash.
units.explain: Computes the encoded length of a string as a JSON-pointer token, counting one extra byte for each tilde or slash. It excludes the terminating NUL and assumes a non-NULL input.
units.sig: static size_t pointer_encoded_length(const unsigned char *string)

units.name: encode_string_as_pointer
units.summary: Writes a JSON-pointer-escaped copy of a source string into caller-provided storage.
units.explain: Writes a JSON-pointer-escaped copy of a source string into caller-provided storage. Slash becomes ~1, tilde becomes ~0, other bytes are copied, and a NUL terminator is appended. No bounds checking is performed.
units.sig: static void encode_string_as_pointer(unsigned char *destination, const unsigned char *source)

units.name: cJSONUtils_FindPointerFromObjectTo
units.summary: Builds a JSON pointer from an ancestor object to a descendant target by recursive child search.
units.explain: Builds a JSON pointer from an ancestor object to a descendant target by recursive child search. - NULL input or target not found: NULL. - Ancestor equals target: allocated empty string. - Array ancestor: prepend slash plus decimal child index. - Object ancestor: prepend slash plus the child key escaped as a pointer token. - Fou…
units.sig: CJSON_PUBLIC(char *) cJSONUtils_FindPointerFromObjectTo(const cJSON * const object, const cJSON * const target)

units.name: get_array_item
units.summary: Returns the child at a zero-based position in an array-like cJSON list by walking next links.
units.explain: Returns the child at a zero-based position in an array-like cJSON list by walking next links. A NULL array or an index past the end yields NULL; no bounds or type check is performed.
units.sig: static cJSON *get_array_item(const cJSON *array, size_t item)

units.name: decode_array_index_from_pointer
units.summary: Parses a decimal array index from the start of a pointer token.
units.explain: Parses a decimal array index from the start of a pointer token. - Leading zero unless token is exactly 0 or followed by slash: reject. - Non-digit before NUL or slash: reject. - Empty token: accepted as index 0. - Overflow: not checked. Writes the parsed size_t on success.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool decode_array_index_from_pointer(const unsigned char * const pointer, size_t * const index)

units.name: pointer lookup
units.summary: Resolves a slash-separated JSON pointer against an object or array, returning the addressed node or NULL; public wrappers select case-insensitive or case-sensitive key matching.
units.explain: Resolves a slash-separated JSON pointer against an object or array, returning the addressed node or NULL; public wrappers select case-insensitive or case-sensitive key matching. - NULL pointer: NULL. - Pointer not starting with slash: return starting node unchanged. - Array token: require a decodable index. - Object token: scan…
units.sig: static cJSON *get_item_from_pointer(cJSON * const object, const char * pointer, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: decode_pointer_inplace
units.summary: Decodes ~0 and ~1 escapes in place in a mutable pointer token.
units.explain: Decodes ~0 and ~1 escapes in place in a mutable pointer token. - NULL input: return immediately. - ~0: write tilde. - ~1: writes slash at the next decoded byte rather than the current one, so the result is not the standard decoded token. - Invalid escape: return early without writing the final NUL terminator.
units.sig: static void decode_pointer_inplace(unsigned char *string)

units.name: detach_item_from_array
units.summary: Detaches the zero-based child from an array-like cJSON list and returns it, or NULL if the position does not exist.
units.explain: Detaches the zero-based child from an array-like cJSON list and returns it, or NULL if the position does not exist. It unlinks the node from the doubly linked list, updates the head and tail links, and clears the detached node's next and prev pointers. The array argument is dereferenced without a NULL check.
units.sig: static cJSON *detach_item_from_array(cJSON *array, size_t which)

units.name: detach_path
units.summary: Splits a path at its last slash, resolves the parent, and detaches the final child.
units.explain: Splits a path at its last slash, resolves the parent, and detaches the final child. - Copy failure, no slash, parent resolution failure, non-container parent, invalid array index, or absent child: NULL. - Array parent: detach by decoded index. - Object parent: detach with the case-insensitive object detach call, so the case-sen…
units.sig: static cJSON *detach_path(cJSON *object, const unsigned char *path, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: object sorting
units.summary: Sorts a cJSON child list by key using recursive merge sort; public wrappers sort objects case-insensitively or case-sensitively.
units.explain: Sorts a cJSON child list by key using recursive merge sort; public wrappers sort objects case-insensitively or case-sensitively. - NULL or single-node list: returned unchanged. - Already strictly increasing list: left unchanged. - Merge: choose first sublist only when comparator is negative, otherwise choose second. - NULL key:…
units.sig: static cJSON *sort_list(cJSON *list, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: compare_json
units.summary: Compares two cJSON trees for structural equality, optionally folding object-key case.
units.explain: Compares two cJSON trees for structural equality, optionally folding object-key case. - NULL operand or differing low-byte type: false. - Numbers: compare integer and epsilon-double values. - Strings: case-sensitive strcmp regardless of the flag. - Arrays: compare children in order and require equal length. - Objects: sort both…
units.sig: static cJSON_bool compare_json(cJSON *a, cJSON *b, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: insert_item_in_array
units.summary: Inserts a new item before the zero-based position in an array-like cJSON list.
units.explain: Inserts a new item before the zero-based position in an array-like cJSON list. - Position equals current length: append via the array add helper. - Position beyond end: return false without inserting. - Position zero: update head. - Other position: link after previous node. Returns true on success and mutates the list.
units.sig: static cJSON_bool insert_item_in_array(cJSON *array, size_t which, cJSON *newitem)

units.name: patch operation decoding
units.summary: Looks up a patch field with the selected key-case mode and decodes the operation name.
units.explain: Looks up a patch field with the selected key-case mode and decodes the operation name. - Lookup delegates to case-sensitive or case-insensitive cJSON object access. - Operation value not a string: INVALID. - Exact lowercase add, remove, replace, move, copy, or test: corresponding opcode. - Missing or unknown value: INVALID.
units.sig: static cJSON *get_object_item(const cJSON * const object, const char* name, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: overwrite_item
units.summary: Replaces a cJSON node's contents with a supplied struct value, freeing the old owned string, value string, and child tree first.
units.explain: Replaces a cJSON node's contents with a supplied struct value, freeing the old owned string, value string, and child tree first. A NULL root is ignored. The function then copies the replacement struct over the root, transferring ownership of the replacement's pointers; it does not free the root node itself.
units.sig: static void overwrite_item(cJSON * const root, const cJSON replacement)

units.name: patch application
units.summary: Applies one JSON Patch operation to a target tree and returns a status code; public wrappers iterate patches and stop at the first nonzero status.
units.explain: Applies one JSON Patch operation to a target tree and returns a status code; public wrappers iterate patches and stop at the first nonzero status. - Non-array patch list: return 1. - Missing or non-string path: status 2. - Invalid op: status 3. - Test: status 0 when addressed value equals patch value, otherwise 1. - Root-path r…
units.sig: static int apply_patch(cJSON *object, const cJSON *patch, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)

units.name: patch composition
units.summary: Builds a patch object and appends it to a patch array; the public wrapper supplies no suffix.
units.explain: Builds a patch object and appends it to a patch array; the public wrapper supplies no suffix. - NULL patch array, operation, or path: return without action. - Patch object creation failure: return without action. - Suffix NULL: add path directly. - Suffix non-NULL: append slash plus pointer-escaped suffix. - Value non-NULL: add…
